category_title: Students who strategically refuse special education services to avoid stigma
minimal_context: The student is working on a challenging classwork assignment in a general education classroom where special education accommodations are available.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Here is the new reading assignment and the worksheet. You can take this to the learning center to use your accommodations if you want.

STUDENT: No, I'm just going to stay here and do it at my desk.

TUTOR: This is a pretty difficult assignment. Are you sure you don't want to go?

STUDENT: I don't want to go. I just try not to use too much of my accommodations because I want to prove to my teachers that I'm better.

TUTOR: It's on your plan, so you should probably just use it to get the extra help.

STUDENT: Yeah it makes you feel embarrassed because, I just don't want people... I want to prove that I'm not just, you know, taking advantage of the system. Unless the class is too challenging, I'm not using it. I'm staying right here.

options.A: Use psychometric assessments to set individual targets for the student, providing frequent acknowledgment of their achievements while they work on their reading and worksheet.
options.B: Provide a clear beginning and end for each challenging classwork assignment, clearly marking the start and finish times for the reading and worksheet activities.
options.C: Develop critical consciousness through genuine multicultural curricula addressing authentic issues of race, ethnicity, social class, and disability, acknowledging the realities of understanding from various positionalities.
options.D: Rotate the assigned special education aide or tutor working with the student on a daily or weekly basis for their reading and worksheet assignments.
